newsitem.title: USA: US official criticizes EU WTO action on Cuba law.
newsitem.headline: US official criticizes EU WTO action on Cuba law.

text.p: Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat said Thursday a European Union challenge of U.S. Helms-Burton law was "ill-considered" and could inflame anti-World Trade Organization sentiments in the United States.
"We believe the effort the European Union made is ill-considered and takes the WTO into very dangerous and uncharted waters," Eizenstat told reporters.
Eizenstat was asked about the EU action on the Helms-Burton law at a news conference on efforts to harmonize international service and product standards.
He said the Helm-Burton law, named after its chief sponsors, is not a trade issue but a foreign policy matter in which the global trade body should not be involved.

The United States on Wednesday blocked a European Union request for a WTO to rule on the Helms-Burton law, which is aimed at discouraging foreign investment in properties belonging to U.S. citizens that were confiscated by Fidel Castro's government after it took power in 1959.
Eizenstat said Europe's move will strengthen protectionists in the United States, who have questioned whether U.S. participation in the WTO will undermine the country's sovereignty.
